FROZEN_TARGET_A.statement: For every integer r>=1, a deterministic algorithm running in time polynomial in the encoded output size produces an HPS-good Ramanujan r-cover of the exact frozen STS31 Levi base.

MINIMAL_SCIENTIFIC_TARGET_B.statement: There exist an explicit unbounded sequence r_k and a deterministic output-polynomial algorithm producing HPS-good r_k-covers of the exact frozen STS31 Levi base.

HPS_ALGORITHMIZATION_AUDIT.external_source: Chris Hall, Doron Puder, William F. Sawin, Ramanujan Coverings of Graphs, Advances in Mathematics 323 (2018), 367-410, DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2017.10.042, arXiv:1506.02335v4 (22 Jul 2026)
HPS_ALGORITHMIZATION_AUDIT.existence_import: Every connected bipartite graph has a Ramanujan r-covering for every r>=1; this is existence, not an efficient selector.
HPS_ALGORITHMIZATION_AUDIT.interlacing_structure: HPS Proposition 4.4 and Corollary 4.5 give real-rooted conditional averages/common-interlacing descent and guarantee that a child labeling exists whose largest root does not exceed the parent average largest root.

factorial_branching_refinement.reason: HPS Remark 4.7 gives an exact factorization of a uniform S_r permutation into at most binom(r,2) rank-1 random swaps, each with constant-size support. For the fixed 465-edge base the resulting interlacing decision depth is O(465*r^2).

root_average_fixed_base_refinement.proof: HPS formula (2.3) expresses the d-matching polynomial as a sum over d-multi-matchings m:E(B)->{0,...,d}. The frozen base has exactly 465 unoriented incidences, so there are at most (d+1)^465 raw edge-count vectors to enumerate and filter by the fixed 186 vertex-capacity inequalities. With d=r-1, this is polynomial in r because 465 is a fixed constant. Each weight W_d(m) is an explicit product/quotient of multinomial/binomial coefficients with polynomial bit length, and the resulting polynomial degree is 186(r-1).

conditional_node_gap.statement: After fixing a prefix of rank-1 random-swap choices on one or more edge permutations, the full S_r symmetry used by the d-multi-matching center formula is broken. No source-bound or independently derived algorithm was obtained that computes every such conditional expected characteristic polynomial, or an equivalent exact branch-selection certificate, in poly(r) time.
conditional_node_gap.why_it_matters: Corollary 4.5 is existential. Algorithmic descent needs an efficiently computable quantity that identifies a good child at every one of O(r^2) decision nodes along one path.

root_comparison.statement: If an exact conditional polynomial of degree O(r) with polynomial-bit rational coefficients were available, comparison of its largest real root with the fixed algebraic threshold rho=sqrt(14)+sqrt(2) can be handled by standard exact real-algebraic/root-isolation methods in polynomial bit complexity. This does not solve conditional-polynomial computation.
root_comparison.alternative_branch_certificate_candidate: Common interlacing suggests that exact evaluation/sign information at the fixed threshold rho, together with equality-safe handling, may suffice to select a child; this is a candidate compression only and was not certified here.

FIXED_BASE_COMPLEXITY_AUDIT.positive_fixed_base_advantage: The fully symmetric unconditional HPS d-matching polynomial is computable in r^O(1) for this exact fixed base by enumerating O(r^465) projected multi-matching vectors.

sources.finding: Existence for arbitrary r and exact polynomial-depth random-swap interlacing representation; no deterministic output-polynomial selector theorem stated.

sources.source: Nikhil Srivastava, Ramanujan Graphs and Interlacing Families, arXiv:2412.20721
sources.finding: States that polynomial-time algorithms for Ramanujan 2-covers or n-covers of arbitrary base graphs are not known and lists polynomial-time finding of the guaranteed covers as an open question; also notes relevant expected characteristic polynomials are #P-hard to compute exactly in the general setting.

sources.source: Michael B. Cohen, Ramanujan Graphs in Polynomial Time, arXiv:1604.03544
sources.finding: Deterministic polynomial construction for bipartite Ramanujan multigraphs via a different efficiently computable interlacing family; not a selector of an HPS cover of this frozen base.

sources.source: Aurelien Gribinski, Adam W. Marcus, arXiv:2108.02534
sources.finding: Polynomial-time biregular bipartite Ramanujan construction, including degree pair (15,3), but not source-bound to the exact fixed-base-cover plus simple+C4-free interface.

sources.source: Approximating the Largest Root and Applications to Interlacing Families, arXiv:1704.03892
sources.finding: Subexponential algorithms from accessible top coefficients; does not give an exact polynomial HPS-cover selector.

Known cyclic/group-based results give randomized or quasi-polynomial almost-Ramanujan constructions in relevant regimes and include limitations for large abelian lifts; they do not satisfy exact target A.

ITERATED_2_LIFT_AUDIT.existence: HPS/MSS existence can be iterated existentially to obtain towers of good 2-covers in the bipartite setting.
ITERATED_2_LIFT_AUDIT.reason: At each growing stage one needs a deterministic polynomial-time selector for a good 2-lift of the current graph. The 2024 survey explicitly records that polynomial-time finding of Ramanujan 2-covers for arbitrary base graphs is not known.
ITERATED_2_LIFT_AUDIT.fixed_first_stage_note: The first 2-lift of the fixed 465-edge STS31 base could be exhaustively searched with a base-dependent constant 2^465 cost, but subsequent stages have Theta(2^k) edges, so analogous exhaustive signing is exponential in current/final output size.

A_VERDICT_RATIONALE: No deterministic output-polynomial selector satisfying all r>=1 was constructed or source-bound.
No unconditional complexity or structural obstruction proving that such a selector cannot exist was established.
The factorial branching objection is insufficient because HPS supplies a polynomial-depth rank-1 random-swap representation.
The general #P-hardness statement is insufficient to falsify the exact fixed-base target because the unconditional center polynomial is polynomially enumerable for this constant-size base.
The remaining exact obstacle is conditional node evaluation after symmetry-breaking partial swap assignments.

CAPTAIN_OBVIOUS_NEXT_MISSING_LINK.statement: Determine whether the conditional expected new-spectrum characteristic polynomial, or an equality-safe exact branch-selection certificate sufficient for HPS common-interlacing descent, can be computed in poly(r) time at every prefix of the frozen O(r^2)-depth random-swap factorization for the fixed STS31 base.
CAPTAIN_OBVIOUS_NEXT_MISSING_LINK.why_minimal: Branch depth, existence, base geometry, cover preservation, reducer stability and structural width consequences are already closed; conditional branch evaluation is the first unclosed algorithmic edge in the direct HPS selector DAG.

NEXT_SINGLE_GATE.scope: Preregister the exact conditional-node computation/branch-certificate problem exposed by this OPEN gate. Do not start it automatically; do not replace A, generate SAT instances, run reducer/treewidth sweeps, or promote H1/H2/H3.
